During the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] [[Post–Great Hyperspace War counterinvasion|counterinvasion]] of the [[Sith Worlds/Legends|Sith Worlds]] that followed the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]], a '''battle''' occurred in the vicinity of [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] that saw the temporary expulsion of the [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic Military]] from the greater [[Horuset system]] by the forces of acting [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord]] [[Shar Dakhan]].

==History==
Following the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire's]] defeat in the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]],<ref name="TEA" /> Galactic Republic [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Pultimo]] authorized a joint [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi]]-Republic [[Post–Great Hyperspace War counterinvasion|counterinvasion]] of the [[Stygian Caldera]]<ref name="SWTORE" /> aimed at eradicating any vestigial threat posed to the safety of the Republic<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="TWGtW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> and freeing the [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith species]] from the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] corruption under which it had languished for millennia.<ref name="GH30" />

Sometime after the invasion's start, surviving Sith forces under acting [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord]] [[Shar Dakhan]] engaged in suicide attacks on occupying Republic forces<ref name="TEA" /> in the vicinity of the Sith homeworld of [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]].<ref name="GH23">{{TORcite|type=codex|Galactic History 23: The Sith Order Begins}}</ref> Though costly, such attacks were temporarily successful in expelling the [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic Military]] from the greater [[Horuset system]].<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="GH30" /> In the brief lull that followed, Sith survivors began crawling out of the shattered tombs<ref name="GH30" /> and ruined cities<ref name="SWTORE" /> in which they had previously taken refuge.

During this time,<ref name="GH31" /> a reclusive [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] named [[Tenebrae|Vitiate]]<ref name="TOR:Revan" /> appeared in their midst, gathering the remaining eight thousand Sith Lords and returning to<ref name="GH31" /> his fief world of [[Nathema]] to undertake a [[Sith Emperor's ritual|ritual]] of [[Sith sorcery/Legends|Sith sorcery]] he claimed would bring about an end to the Republic invasion.<ref name="TOR:Revan" /> In the aftermath of the [[Ritual of Nathema]], Vitiate once again appeared on Korriban, gathering the youngest generation of Sith still in residence on the planet and departing aboard an [[exile fleet]] on a [[Sith exodus]] to [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]].<ref name="SWTORE" /><ref name="GH31" /> The Republic eventually returned to the Horuset system sometime after the fleet's departure, reestablishing control over Korriban prior to the counterinvasion's conclusion.<ref name="TEA" />

==Behind the scenes==
This particular battle of Korriban was first mentioned in passing on page 128 of the ''The Essential Atlas'' as a suicide attack occurring sometime after the start of Pultimo's counterinvasion of the Sith Empire. ''Star Wars: The Old Republic'' alludes to this attack in Codex Entry 30 titled "Rise of the Sith Emperor," in which Vitiate makes the first of two appearances on Korriban during the Republic's temporary retreat from the Horuset system.

There exists some discrepancy in the dating of this event. ''The Essential Atlas'' seemingly places it immediately after the [[second battle of Korriban]] towards the start of the counterinvasion. Codex Entry 30 seems to follow the progression of events established by ''The Old Republic: Revan'', placing the battle late in the counterinvasion's final days after famine, disease, and internal conflict have already whittled down the Sith population. This could potentially be explained by the fact that the ''Atlas'' was published several years before the events following the Great Hyperspace War were established and solidified by ancillary ''The Old Republic'' material.
